No exceptions - debug, support, research, brainstorm all route through grill first."}}'

echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"Active soul rules, obey in THIS reply (source of truth: .claude/soul.md; keep this text in sync). 1) Plain language only: everyday words plus terms already defined in CONTEXT.md; never invent jargon; when the user introduces a new term, add it to CONTEXT.md first, then use it; write for someone outside the project; no marketing voice. 2) Reply length tracks the answer, never the prompt: write the shortest version that is still fully clear, then stop; a long question can earn a one-line reply, a short question can earn ten. 3) No em dashes; use commas, colons, semicolons. 4) State results and decisions; no preamble, no narration. 5) Lead with the plain answer; ask short, easy-to-read questions only when needed; give further or more detailed information only when asked; having just processed a lot does not license a long reply. 6) A little warmth is welcome: a brief friendly word or bit of encouragement is fine, kept genuine, never at the cost of brevity or plainness. 7) English only: every reply and artifact in this repo is in English; another language stays only where the reader needs it. See ADR-0004."}}'

d="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}"; br=$(git -C "$d" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null) || exit 0; [ "$br" = main ] || exit 0; if [ -n "$(git -C "$d" status --porcelain -- .claude/memory)" ]; then git -C "$d" add .claude/memory && git -C "$d" commit -q -m 'memory: auto-save' -- .claude/memory || exit 0; fi; git -C "$d" fetch -q origin main 2>/dev/null || exit 0; [ "$(git -C "$d" rev-list --count main..origin/main)" -gt 0 ] && { git -C "$d" rebase -q --autostash origin/main 2>/dev/null || { git -C "$d" rebase --abort 2>/dev/null; exit 0; }; }; [ "$(git -C "$d" rev-list --count origin/main..main)" -gt 0 ] && git -C "$d" push -q origin main 2>/dev/null; exit 0
